title: a place's names that make different requests are each asked
line: the runner asks a name of a place only when the request it makes differs from every request already made on the run, not only the one before it: names that read as different counties are each asked and the run stops at the first that gets a hit, a name that repeats an earlier request is logged as tried and its request not made again; a name whose request the source did not answer, or that repeats such a request, is logged unanswered beside the names tried, the name answered with nothing is not, and the step stays runnable so the next turn asks again

steps.say: the 1950 census fetch step for Robert Edgar Davidson, its place carrying the citation's own string, then the county the town sat in before Nassau County was cut from Queens County in 1899, then the town as the resolver names it: the first and the third read as the same county, the second as another

value: Town of Hempstead < Nassau County < New York < United States

citation.value: National Archives at Washington, DC; Washington, D.C.; Seventeenth Census of the United States, 1950

steps.say: the real census connector: Nassau then Queens are two requests, each asked: the site does not answer Nassau's (the harness's stand-in for a holder that does not answer) and answers Queens's with nothing; the town's resolved name makes Nassau's request again and is not asked

answers.error: the harness's stand-in for no answer: timed out

expect.why: two requests go out, one per county, neither getting a hit; the third name repeats the first's request, which is not the one just before it, and is the only name left unasked; all three are on the tried list, and the two whose request the site did not answer, Nassau's and the town's that repeats it, are unanswered: Queens's answer of nothing is an answer
a run that left names unanswered never asked the step's fields in full: the next turn asks the census site again
